title: New Zealand domestic travel is socially motivated and culturally selective, with cost, health, and weather limiting future trips
source_unit: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment Domestic Visitor Survey, October 2025 wave
geography: New Zealand; population-representative domestic visitors and planned domestic travellers, weighted to 2023 Census age, gender, region, and ethnicity

denominator.unit: Weighted Domestic Visitor Survey respondents; survey sample size not stated in the top-line release

overnight_trip_participation.unit: percent taking at least one domestic overnight trip

overnight_median_trip_count.unit: median number of domestic overnight trips among relevant respondents

overnight_median_nights.unit: median nights for domestic overnight trips

day_trip_participation.unit: percent taking at least one qualifying domestic day trip

motivations.value: Overnight: visit family/friends 36%, relax/unwind 22%, bond with travel companions 20%; day: visit family/friends 29%, relax/unwind 20%, bond with travel companions 18%

mechanism.value: Domestic travel is partly a social-reproduction activity—family, friends, relaxation, and companion bonding—not only a leisure purchase; trip frequency and duration remain modest

observations.method: MBIE Domestic Visitor Survey October 2025 wave covering overnight and qualifying day trips; data weighted by age, gender, region, and ethnicity to match 2023 Census population characteristics.
observations.uncertainty: The top-line release does not state the sample size. Trip definitions are specific: overnight means at least one night; day trips require travel at least 40 km one way or air/ferry travel outside the usual work/living area. Multiple-response totals need not sum to 100%.
observations.subgroup: New Zealand residents reporting past domestic overnight or day travel during April-October 2025.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported travel may include family obligations rather than discretionary leisure; a median of two trips does not reveal inequality by income, disability, region, household structure, or transport access.

observations.period: April-October 2025; cultural and outdoor activities on domestic overnight trips

denominator.unit: Weighted domestic overnight-trip respondents; sample size not stated in top-line release

walked_hiked.unit: percent of domestic overnight trips involving walking or hiking

no_physical_activity.unit: approximate percent of domestic overnight trips reporting no physical activity

museum_gallery_visit.unit: percent of domestic overnight trips involving a museum or gallery visit

maori_cultural_site_visit.unit: percent of domestic overnight trips involving a Māori cultural-site visit

mechanism.value: Domestic travel creates a selective culture-and-nature bundle: outdoor activity is more common than museum/gallery visits, while Māori cultural sites reach a smaller but visible share of overnight trips

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from MBIE DVS October 2025 top-line activity and experience measures; activities allow multiple responses.
observations.uncertainty: The measures are trip-level survey reports and do not establish spending, attendance duration, cultural meaning, provider revenue, authenticity, or community benefit. Multiple activities can be selected for one trip.
observations.subgroup: Domestic overnight trips reported by New Zealand residents in the April-October 2025 reference period.
observations.counterinterpretation: The activity mix reflects destination supply, itinerary design, weather, transport, family composition, and question interpretation; lower Māori cultural-site reach does not by itself indicate lower interest or access.

observations.period: October 2025-April 2026; planned domestic travel and barriers

denominator.unit: Weighted respondents with planned domestic travel; sample size not stated in top-line release

planned_overnight_travel.unit: percent expecting at least one domestic overnight trip in the next six months

planned_day_travel.unit: percent expecting at least one domestic day trip in the next six months

overnight_cost_barrier.unit: percent citing being too expensive as a barrier to planned overnight travel

day_cost_barrier.unit: percent citing being too expensive as a barrier to planned day travel

overnight_health_barrier.unit: percent citing illness or poor health as a barrier to planned overnight travel

day_weather_barrier.unit: percent citing weather as a barrier to planned day travel

decision_routes.value: Destination websites 38%, friends/family with destination experience 37%, general internet search or other websites 33%

mechanism.value: Stated future demand exceeds realized recent participation, but conversion is constrained by price, health, weather, and commitments; discovery relies on both official/destination information and trusted social recommendations

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from MBIE DVS October 2025 planned-travel, barrier, and decision-making questions; multiple responses are permitted.
observations.uncertainty: Intentions are not bookings or completed trips. Barrier percentages use the relevant planned-travel subgroup, and the top-line release does not disclose denominators or subgroup uncertainty; weather and illness may be episodic rather than structural.
observations.subgroup: New Zealand residents reporting planned domestic overnight or day travel for October 2025-April 2026.
observations.counterinterpretation: High intention may reflect aspirational reporting; cost may be a proxy for time, distance, accommodation, fuel, or household commitments, while social recommendation does not establish actual destination choice or satisfaction.

Official October 2025 DVS top-line findings, definitions, weighting, travel, activity, satisfaction, intentions, barriers, and decision sources.

boundary: This record adds a New Zealand domestic-mobility, cultural-activity, social-motivation, and travel-cost layer. It does not establish household-level affordability, regional distribution, cultural meaning, Māori community benefit, causal travel effects, or booked/completed future trips.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official MBIE/TEIC Domestic Visitor Survey October 2025 key-highlights PDF reviewed for trip definitions, weighting, past travel, motivations, cultural activities, satisfaction, intentions, barriers, decision routes, and mean/median limitations.
